channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Ex-UK water boss charged in plot to 'manipulate' test results
item.description: Former Southern Water CEO Matthew Wright has been charged with conspiring to manipulate water quality tests, with a judge describing the allegations as involving “carefully planned and extensive fraud and dishonesty at a high level.” Ex-UK water boss charged in plot to 'manipulate' test results.

item.title: Iran Executes Man Charged Over January Protests As Death Row Inmates Stage Hunger Strike
item.description: Iran has executed Mehdi Khaneki, a young man convicted on charges tied to anti-government protests that swept across the country in January. The execution came as some 1,500 death row inmates at the prison continued a hunger strike demanding an end to executions. Iran Executes Man Charged Over January Protests As Death Row Inmates Stage Hunger Strike.

item.title: Make in U.S. by August 2028 or pay up to 200% duty, Trump tells generic drugmakers
item.description: Effective August 1, 2026, all generic drugs being brought into the United States will continue to have a tariff of zero per cent for a two-year period of time, after which the tariff will be raised to 100% for a one-year period of time, and 200% thereafter, said Donald Trump Make in U. S. by August 2028 or pay up to 200% duty, Trump tells generic drugmakers.

item.title: Canada cancels joint bridge-opening celebration with US amid trade tensions
item.description: The ribbon-cutting celebration of the Gordie Howe International Bridge is no longer taking place after Trump announced a 50% tariff on Canadian goodsA planned joint US-Canada ceremony Friday celebrating the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, is no longer expected to take place after Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on most Canadian goods.

item.title: Iran Continues Executions Amid Protest By Death Row Inmates
item.description: Iran executed a man it accused of carrying out "operational actions" during nationwide protests at the start of the year as the country's leadership ratchets up its crackdown on dissent, sparking a hunger strike among hundreds of death row inmates. Iran Continues Executions Amid Protest By Death Row Inmates.

item.description: US secretary of state says international community should ‘join forces’ against authoritarian Ortega regimeNicaragua’s congress, controlled by the country’s long-serving president, Daniel Ortega, has announced a “work plan” to implement the authoritarian leader’s order that the country should no longer hold elections. item.title: Rubio Says Iran-Backed Houthis' Red Sea Blockade 'Problematic'
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ‌said on July 22 that a naval blockade of the Red Sea by Yemen’s Houthi rebels would be “problematic,” as the widening conflict with Iran disrupted two of the world’s most important energy chokepoints. Rubio Says Iran-Backed Houthis' Red Sea Blockade 'Problematic'.

item.title: Sperm whales change ‘vowel’ sounds when boats are nearby, scientists discover
item.description: Researchers listening off the Caribbean island of Dominica found variations in the mammals’ audible clicks when marine traffic was closeSperm whales produce a specific pattern of clicking noises when they hear the noise of boats, researchers have found. The pattern is so distinct that the scientists who identified it said they can now use it to predict when ships are nearby.

item.title: Deadly Afghanistan floods kill at least 26 as aid agencies race to reach survivors
item.description: Flash floods have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in the mountainous province of Nuristan, where homes, markets and roads were swept away and search teams continued looking for people reported missing. Deadly Afghanistan floods kill at least 26 as aid agencies race to reach survivors.

item.title: US, Ukraine Reach Breakthrough Agreement On Drone Cooperation
item.description: The US and Ukraine have signed a statement of intent creating the first formal framework for cooperation on military drones, paving the way for Ukrainian combat drones to be exported to the US for testing and potentially future joint production. US, Ukraine Reach Breakthrough Agreement On Drone Cooperation.

item.title: Michelin-starred restaurant owner in South Korea faces jail over ant dessert
item.description: Prosecutors seek a one-year sentence and heavy fine after chef garnished dish with insects not approved for consumptionProsecutors in South Korea have asked a court to sentence the owner of a Michelin-starred restaurant to one year in prison for serving a dessert topped with ants, an insect not approved for consumption under local food safety law. Michelin-starred restaurant owner in South Korea faces jail over ant dessert.

item.title: Ukraine Hits Russian Retailer Wildberries' Warehouses Again Amid Accusations It Supplies Military
item.description: The Ukrainian military struck warehouses belonging to Russia's largest online retailer, Wildberries, in the third such attack in a week, as Kyiv continues to expand its retaliatory long-range strike campaign in an effort to force Moscow into negotiations. item.title: Rubio Says Iran Not Serious About Diplomacy, Warns ASEAN On Hormuz Threat
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has warned that Iran's challenge to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz threatened not only global trade but also risked setting a dangerous precedent for Asia's contested maritime routes. Rubio Says Iran Not Serious About Diplomacy, Warns ASEAN On Hormuz Threat.

item.title: How Australia resisted PRC economic coercion: lessons for others
